title: Plan Advent
hookLine: decide ahead how you'll wait this year
tomorrow: giving up chocolate for Lent: is that really the whole idea?

cards: December. The holiday aisle shows up early, and the calendar fills fast: parties, shopping, travel, a school concert, one more gift to wrap.
A month like that runs itself unless somebody decides otherwise, and it has to be decided before it starts. Planning it while it still feels far away sounds odd. That's exactly when it works.
Some churches give the weeks before Christmas a name and a purpose of their own. They call it Advent.

teach.b: Advent is a season of waiting and getting ready.
Its theme comes from a voice in Isaiah, in the King James Bible: “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
Mark's Gospel hears that voice in John the Baptist, right at the start of Jesus' story: “Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.”

teach.h: A ROAD BUILT BEFORE THE TRAVELER.
teach.b: A road is built before the traveler arrives, not while he's knocking. That's the case for planning Advent early.
Churches that keep the season describe a waiting that faces two ways: back toward the birth remembered at Christmas, and forward to Christ coming again. They keep it differently.
Some households light candles on an Advent wreath, one more each week. Some open an Advent calendar, a door a day.

teach.h: READ ONE, SKIP ONE, GIVE ONE.
teach.b: Some read a short passage each evening. Orthodox Christians keep a season of fasting before Christmas. Some churches don't mark Advent at all and simply keep Christmas.
Where the season matters, a plan helps, because December won't leave room by itself. One thing to read or pray.
One thing to go without. One way to give. Small enough to survive the parties, and portable enough to travel.

how: Churches that keep Advent mark the weeks before Christmas as a season of waiting: some households light an Advent wreath, open an Advent calendar or read a short daily passage, and Orthodox Christians keep a fast before Christmas.

o: deciding ahead how to wait and get ready for Christmas
choosing which carols the choir sings on Christmas Eve
booking the family's holiday travel well in advance

games.q: getting the road ready — tap the pairs.
p: back to the birth, forward to his coming

s: Advent is just another name for the Christmas holidays
it's the season of waiting and getting ready before Christmas.
prepare ye the way of the LORD comes from Isaiah
Mark's Gospel hears the same voice in John the Baptist.
every church keeps Advent the same way
some light a wreath, Orthodox Christians keep a fast, and some churches don't mark it at all.

games.q: your mom's December already holds a party almost every weekend. she wants to keep Advent this year but says there's no room. what does today suggest?
o: pick one small thing now, before the parties set the pace.
wait until December and see what time is left over.
cancel the parties; Advent means no celebrating at all.
games.why: prepare ye the way: the road is built before the traveler arrives. a small plan made early survives a full month.

practice: Say your Advent plan out loud in three short sentences: one thing I'll read, one thing I'll go without, one way I'll give. Say it slowly enough to hear whether it's small enough to survive December.
If it isn't, cut it in half and say it again.

wordCard.voice: Plan Advent. Decide ahead how you'll wait this year, so the road is ready before the season arrives.

orig.note: Latin for a coming or arrival, the source of the name Advent.

carryVoice: Your line: prepare the way. A road gets built before the traveler comes, not while he's knocking. Until tomorrow.
